newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close higher, but trade seen edgy.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close higher, but trade seen edgy.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed up on Friday eyeing a strong start on Wall Street after a favourable January U.S. employment report. But the tone was still somewhat nervous and dealers saw no clear trend short-term.
The general index rose 2.98 points, 0.63 percent, to 475.41 and the Ibex added 34.26 points, 0.63 percent, to 5,449.76.
Endesa rose 90 pesetas to 9,440 rebounding on technical factors. News that new chairman is Martin Villa, replacing Fuster, was widely expected, dealers said.
The rebound in Endesa was contrasted in weakness in Iberdrola, which shed 30 pesetas to 1,605, consolidating recent gains, dealers said.
Telefonica continued strong amid the sale of the government's last stake, adding 25 pesetas to 3,395.

Medium term the prospects for the bourse are still good, but short term volatility will continue, with foreign investors trimming positions. Nevertheless, domestic funds are still flowing in, they added.
"Although we've ended positively, the comeback is lower than on other bourses...The base is still cautious," said one trader.
